newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thais, Singapore pursue workers pact for Indochina.
newsitem.headline: Thais, Singapore pursue workers pact for Indochina.

text.p: Visiting Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong said on Wednesday his country and Thailand would work together to promote human resource development in Indochina.
Goh told a news conference Thailand was well placed to take advantage of rapid economic growth in Indochina.
"Thailand can provide infrastructure to these countries and Singapore can work with Thailand to provide development on the Mekong region," Goh said.
Singapore and Thailand on Monday signed a bilateral agreement to launch their Third Country Training Programme (TCTP) in Laos, Vietnam and Cambodia.
TCTP calls for the two countries to pool resources and share their development expertise with neighbouring developing countries especially Cambodia, Laos and Burma.
Goh downplayed the possiblity of Thailand competing with Singapore in becoming a future regional shipping hub.
"Singapore will continue to be the hub port but Thailand will become an export port for mainland China," he said.
But Goh expressed his confidence in the Thai economy and hailed a Thai-Singapore industrial estate joint venture signed during his visit.

JTC International Pte Ltd, a wholly-owned unit of Jurong Town Corp of Singapore, teamed up with Eastern Sugar Co Ltd of Thailand in building an 18 billion baht ($720 million) industrial estate in south eastern Thailand.
The venture was the biggest Thai-Singapore joint venture in the past several years.
Goh, accompanied by a large group of Singapore businessmen, arrived in Bangkok on Monday for a three-day visit. ($1 = 25 baht)
